## Read this first

**The de-identification benchmark on i2b2/n2c2 still has not been run.** The
harness and dataset adapter are included and tested, but that corpus is released
only under a Data Use Agreement and was not available. Every de-identification
number published (F1 0.933 rule-only, 0.922 with NER) is on a **synthetic**
corpus - a regression gate, not evidence of real-world accuracy. The default
`DeidEngine` does **not** detect names or street addresses; enable the opt-in NER
recognizer for those.

Other limits: providers are tested against mocked SDKs and models in CI; the UMLS
`map()` call is unverified against the live service; the groundedness check is a
word-overlap heuristic.

**Behaviour changes since 0.5.0 that can change your output** (each fixes a defect):
- The default terminology guardrail now returns a **warning** ("unverifiable") for
  a code its small bundled subset cannot confirm, where 0.5.0 returned a **block**
  ("does not exist"). A block now needs a backend that is authoritative for that
  system.
- `DATE_SHIFT` now redacts non-date identifiers beside dates; 0.5.0 raised an
  error on such a document.
- Run manifests now keep token-count settings such as `max_tokens` instead of
  `[REDACTED]`; credentials are still redacted.
- Config validation now reports unknown or missing step parameters and off-site
  components under a local-only policy up front.

## What is new since 0.5.0

The `openbtk` command line (`list`, `validate`, `run`, `deid`, `replay`, `doctor`),
clinical QA (MedQA / MedMCQA formats) and groundedness evaluation with eval
manifests, guides and a full API reference, and eight tutorial notebooks executed
in CI. Six core dependencies; everything else is an optional extra.

```bash
pip install "openbtk[text]"
openbtk doctor
```

Full detail: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/openbtk/openbtk-core/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
Docs: <https://openbtk.org/openbtk-core/>.
